title.en: Tyr the One-Handed: The God of Oaths Who Fed the Wolf
title.zh: 獨臂的提爾：以誓言為職、曾餵養巨狼之神

region.en: Tyr's courts and the wolf's island (symbolic pin at Lake Viborg, Denmark)
region.zh: 提爾的法庭與巨狼之島（象徵性定位於丹麥維堡湖）

texts.period: Gylfaginning c. 1220-1230 (older material); Lokasenna st. 37-40; Hymiskvida; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to, GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 25; Lokasenna st. 37-40; Hymiskvida; critical ed. Faulkes (1987)

texts.license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916; Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Tyr is the boldest and most courageous of the gods, and it is well for men of victory to call on him: 'it is proven that he rules over victory in battle'. His signature is his missing right hand - lost to the wolf Fenrir's bite when the other gods refused to pledge their own. In Lokasenna, when Loki taunts him - 'I have your hand, the wolf's snare' - Tyr answers with the oath-keeper's grief: 'I lost my hand, the wolf's snare, and grief have I got; the wolf stays bound, and I stay wretched'. And his deepest service is forgotten by all: he is Hymir's son, and it was Tyr who knew the giant's hall and led Thor to the mile-deep kettle. The record is the profile of law's god: the hand of the oath is the hand the wolf ate.
summary.zh: 提爾是諸神中最勇敢、最堅毅者，欲求戰勝者宜呼其名：「確切可知，他掌管戰鬥中的勝利」。其標誌是缺失的右手——當眾神皆不肯以手作保時，他的手被巨狼芬里爾咬去。在《洛基的吵罵》中，洛基譏諷他——「我握有你的手，那狼的鎖鏈」——提爾以守誓者的悲傷作答：「我失了手，成了狼的鎖鏈，我滿懷哀傷；狼被縛住，而我淒苦度日」。而他最深的功勞卻被眾神遺忘：他本是巨人希米爾之子，正是他知道巨人大廳之路，引索爾取回那口深達一里的巨釜。此記錄是法律之神的肖像：誓言之手，正是被狼吃掉的那隻手。

texts.canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Gylfaginning's profile is brief and exact: Tyr is the boldest and most courageous of the gods, and he has great authority over victory in battle; 'it is well for men of valour to call on him'. His other name is 'the one-handed god', and the reason is the wolf: 'when the Aesir enticed Fenrir to let himself be bound with the chain Gleipnir, the wolf did not believe them to be minded to loose him till they laid Tyr's hand in his mouth as a pledge; and when the Aesir would not loose him, then he bit the hand off at the wrist - the place is called the wolf's joint? - and Tyr is one-handed and is not called a reconciler of men'. The prose adds the etymological point: the god of the oath is the god whose pledge-body is broken.

Lokasenna's flyting gives the grief its voice. Loki taunts: 'Be silent, Tyr! Thine hand? ' - the verses: 'I have thy hand, the snare of the wolf, and my son? ' - Loki claims credit for the binding and for the wolf's kinship? - the exchange: Loki says 'I was the father of the wolf? ' - no: Loki jeers 'thy hand could never hold aught', and Tyr answers: 'I lost my hand, the wolf's snare, and grief have I got; the wolf stays bound, and I stay wretched' - and then the second blow: Loki charges Tyr with cuckolding his wife, and Tyr falls silent - the oath-keeper's silence is the flyting's judgment that his private life cannot match his public honor.

The forgotten service is the kettle-quest's frame. In Hymiskvida, it is Tyr who offers to fetch the mile-deep kettle from the giant Hymir - 'for Hymir my father dwells there' - the law-god is the giant's son, and his kinship is the expedition's passport; he lifts the kettle-lid by its ring while Thor carries the vessel. The profile's cultural functions are the doctrine of pledged collateral (the god of oaths literally loses the body-part that secures them) and the paradox of law's kinships (the legal god is half giant - law's passport is a border-family). The etymology 'Tiwaz' ties him to the Indo-European sky-father (cf. Zeus, deus, Jupiter) - the oldest layer of the pantheon, and in the Norse material the god who has been overtaken by Odin and Thor in cult, surviving as the memory of what an oath costs.

For the atlas, the record anchors the sacrificial-office family: the god whose office is embodied (the hand as the pledge) - answering the Greek Zeus Horkios and the Roman Fides: each a deity of the sworn word; the Norse one pays for his office in flesh.

functions: Doctrine of pledged collateral: the oath-god's hand is the pledge the wolf ate
Office embodied in flesh: victory-law and oath-keeping carried on a one-armed body
Law's border-kinship: the legal god is the giant Hymir's son - law's passport is a border-family
Cult-history datum: the Indo-European sky-father (Tiwaz) demoted in Norse cult, surviving as oath-memory

The wolf bit off his hand at the wrist when the gods would not loose the chain, and Tyr is one-handed and is not called a reconciler of men. At the flyting Loki jeered at the empty sleeve; Tyr answered: 'I lost my hand, the wolf's snare, and grief have I got; the wolf stays bound, and I stay wretched.'

title.en: Heimdall the White: Nine Mothers, Gold Teeth and the Horn That Wakes the Worlds
title.zh: 白神海姆達爾：九位母親、金齒與喚醒萬界的號角

region.en: Himinbjorg at Bifrost's edge (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 畢弗羅斯特橋頭的海姆比歐堡（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: Gylfaginning c. 1220-1230 (older material); Vafthrudnismal st. 27-29, 39; Lokasenna; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to, GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 27; Vafthrudnismal st. 27-29, 39; critical ed. Faulkes (1987)

texts.license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916; Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Heimdall is the white god, great and holy, born of nine mothers who are nine sisters - the wave-maidens, per Vafthrudnismal's riddle. His teeth are gold; he needs less sleep than a bird; he sees a hundred leagues by night as by day and hears the grass grow and the wool on the sheep. He guards the sky-bridge with the horn Gjallarhorn, whose blast wakes every world; he opposes Loki (and will kill him and be killed at Ragnarok); and in Rigspula he is the ancestor-father of the social estates. The record is the profile of the watchman-god: the senses of a frontier, the birth of nine waves, the horn of the last alarm.
summary.zh: 海姆達爾是白神，偉大而神聖，由九位彼此為姐妹的母親所生——據《瓦夫特魯德尼爾之歌》之謎，她們正是九位浪之侍女。他生有金齒；所需睡眠比鳥還少；晝夜皆能目視百里之遙，能聽見草的生長與羊背上的羊毛。他守護天橋，手持號角加拉德——其聲一響，萬界皆醒；他與洛基勢不兩立（末日之戰中二人同歸於盡）；在《里格詩篇》中他更是三階層的共同始祖。此記錄是守望之神的肖像：邊境的感官、九道浪濤的誕生，以及最後警報的號角。

texts.canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The profile's strangest datum is his birth. Gylfaginning: 'nine mothers bore him, and all were sisters'; Vafthrudnismal's riddle supplies the identity: Odin asks 'whence came Heimdall, high-born, into the world?' and the giant answers in kenning-code - 'nine children the wave-maiden? ' - the verses: 'he was born of nine sisters, at the world's edge, of the wave-vaunted? one' - the nine sisters are the nine daughters of Aegir and Ran, the wave-maidens: the watchman is the sea's child, born at the world's rim, of the same water that rings Midgard.

The senses are his office: gold teeth; sleep less than a bird; sight of a hundred leagues night and day; hearing of the grass growing and the wool on the sheep's back; and the horn Gjallarhorn, kept in Himinbjorg at the bridge's edge, whose blast wakes every world - Snorri adds that Mimir's head? - no: the horn is also the trumpet of Ragnarok (Völuspá: 'Heimdall blows his horn aloft, men's road? - the sibyl hears it from the top of the tree'), and his counterpart is Loki: enmity between them is old (Lokasenna accuses Heimdall of drink-greed and back-stabbing prudence), and at Ragnarok the two kill each other - the watchman and the thief die in the same stroke.

His third office is social: in Rigspula he travels as Rig and fathers the three estates - thrall, freeman, noble - and the young king Kon, so that the class-system itself descends from the watchman's bed. The record's cultural functions are the frontier-senses doctrine (the guardian as a personified border-sensorium: sight, hearing, sleeplessness, teeth of gold - the god as infrastructure) and the wave-birth doctrine (the sea as the watchman's mother - the boundary made flesh). And his death at Loki's hand makes the profile eschatological: the alarm-system's final act is its own extinction, horn and thief dying together.

In the atlas, the record anchors the sentinel-god family (the Greek Hermes of the boundaries, the Chinese door-gods, the Roman Janus): each a guardian of crossings; the Norse one is distinctive in being born of the sea at the world's edge and in being scheduled to die with the very thief he watches.

The profile's nine-mothers doctrine completes the cosmology: the nine wave-maidens of Aegir and Ran as the watchman's mothers - the sea's daughters bearing the guardian of the sky-bridge - so the frontier between worlds is born from the sea itself. And the death-appointment completes the office: Heimdall and Loki, watchman and thief, kill each other at Ragnarok - the alarm-system's final act is its own extinction, the horn's last blast and the thief's last stroke in the same moment. The record thus anchors the sentinel-god family: the guardian born of the boundary's water, sensing the world's smallest motions, and scheduled to die with the boundary's breaker.

functions: Frontier-senses doctrine: the guardian as personified border-sensorium (sight, hearing, sleeplessness, gold teeth)
Wave-birth doctrine: nine wave-maiden mothers at the world's rim - the boundary made flesh
Watchman's eschatology: the horn of the last alarm, dying with the thief he watches
Social paternity: the class-system descending from the watchman's travels (Rigspula)

title.en: Loki's Kin: The Trickster's Family and the Monster Brood
title.zh: 洛基的親族：詭計者的家族與怪物之群

region.en: Asgard's walls and Jotunheim (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 阿斯加德城牆與約頓海姆（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: Gylfaginning c. 1220-1230 (older material); Lokasenna st. 9; Hyndluljod st. 29-31; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to, GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Snorri, Gylfaginning chs. 33-34; Lokasenna st. 9; Hyndluljod st. 29-31; critical ed. Faulkes (1987)

texts.license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916; Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Loki is the son of the giant Farbauti ('dangerous striker') and Laufey ('leafy isle'), brother of Helblindi and Byleistr; Snorri calls him 'the calumniator and cheat of the gods', handsome and fair of face but evil in disposition, and 'the causer of? ' - the father of the lie. His children with Angrboda are the myth's doom-clock: Fenrir the wolf, Jormungand the serpent, Hel the half-dead girl; and by his wife Sigyn, the sons Narfi and Vali whose entrails bind him. And in Lokasenna's opening he is revealed as Odin's blood-brother - sworn in the morning of time, before the gods' order existed. The record is the genealogy of the trickster as the pantheon's internal border: kin to giants, brother to Odin, father to the world's end.
summary.zh: 洛基是巨人法爾鮑蒂（「危險的擊打者」）與勞菲（「繁茂之島」）之子，海爾布林迪與布萊斯耶爾的兄弟；斯諾里稱他為「諸神的誹謗者與欺詐者」，面容俊美而心地邪惡，是「謊言之父」。他與安格爾波達所生的子女是神話的末日時鐘：巨狼芬里爾、大蛇耶夢加得、半死的少女海爾；他與妻子西格恩所生的納爾菲與瓦利，其腸索日後成為捆縛他的繩索。而《洛基的吵罵》開篇揭示他竟與奧丁結為血盟兄弟——在遠古時光、神界秩序尚未建立之前。此記錄呈現詭計者的譜系：他既是神界的內部邊界——巨人一族之親、奧丁血誓之弟、末日之子的父親。

texts.canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Gylfaginning's dossier opens with the parentage: Loki is the son of Farbauti the giant and Laufey, 'who is counted among the goddesses'? - the text: 'Laufey or Nal is his mother, and Byleistr and Helblindi are his brothers'; and the portrait: 'Loki is handsome and fair of face, but evil in disposition, and very changeable of mood? ' - the prose: 'he surpasses all men in the art of cunning, called the sly one? ' - the dossier reads: 'the calumniator and cheat of the gods, the father of the monster-fish? - the serpent? - Hel and the wolf and, further, the causer of all misfortune among gods and men'. The dossier's punch: Loki is the god-company's own member - 'he is counted among the Aesir' - because of his oath of blood-brotherhood: in Lokasenna's opening, Loki reminds Odin - 'remember, Odin, in the morning of time? we two mixed our blood together; then you said you would never taste ale unless it were brought to us both' - the blood-drinking pact that made the trickster a god's brother by the oldest ritual the north knows.

The brood is the myth's eschatology in genealogy. With the giantess Angrboda, Loki fathered the wolf Fenrir, the serpent Jormungand and Hel; Snorri's chapter reads the family as a prophecy: the three children are the materials of the doom (the wolf to swallow Odin, the serpent to kill Thor, Hel to keep Baldr). By his wife Sigyn he had the sons whose bodies become his binding - Narfi and Vali, one killed by the gods, the other's entrails made into the fetter that holds Loki to the rock. The genealogy thus runs from trickster to catastrophe in one generation: his love-life is the myth's weapon-manufacture.

The record's cultural functions are the internal-border doctrine (the pantheon's trickster is kin to its enemies and brother to its king - the oath-economy's cost made visible) and the lineage-of-doom doctrine (the myth-world's evil is familial, not foreign: the monsters are Loki's children, raised in Asgard itself). And the status is legally precise: Loki is not a giant among the gods nor a god among giants, but a sworn kinsman - the member whose membership is a contract, which is why the flyting is possible (a blood-brother may insult) and why the binding is a family matter (his wife Sigyn holds the bowl). In the atlas, the record anchors the trickster-kinship family (the Greek Hermes, son of Zeus; the Chinese Monkey, made a god by appointment): each a trickster inside the pantheon; the Norse one is unique in being bound by blood-oath to the king and in manufacturing the apocalypse as paternity.

functions: Internal-border doctrine: the trickster is kin to the enemies and blood-brother to the king
Lineage-of-doom: the monsters are Loki's children, raised in Asgard itself
Blood-oath economy: membership as contract - insultable, bindable, family-cared-for
Weapon-manufacture as paternity: his love-life produces the doom-clock

passages.text: Loki is the son of the giant Farbauti and of Laufey; his brothers are Byleistr and Helblindi. He is handsome and fair of face, but evil in disposition and very changeable; he surpasses all men in cunning, and is the calumniator and cheat of the gods, and the causer of all misfortune among gods and men.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 33 (Brodeur 1916); not verbatim.

passages.text: By the giantess Angrboda he fathered the wolf Fenrir, the serpent Jormungand and Hel; and by his wife Sigyn, the sons whose entrails became the fetter that binds him. He is counted among the Aesir - for in the morning of time, he and Odin mixed their blood together as sworn brothers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Snorri, Gylfaginning chs. 33-34, and Lokasenna st. 9 (Brodeur; Bellows); not verbatim.
